# Treemap syntax

<!-- Generated by tools/gen-grammar from packages/diagram-treemap/grammar/treemap.ebnf. Do not edit: run `pnpm gen:grammar`. -->

Treemap syntax (R-PARSE-9, D54): the normative grammar of `treemap` diagrams.

The hand-written parser in `src/parser/` implements it; `tools/gen-grammar` builds a reference
parser, a sentence generator, highlighters and the syntax reference page from it. mermaid@12
decides what is valid, this file is fixed to match, and the parser must match this file
(DESIGN §4.4). mermaid@12 parsed treemap with Langium (`treemap.langium` in
`@mermaid-js/parser`, which does not import `common.langium`); the rules below are its token
rules, in its order, and its grammar.

**Lexer input.** The lexer reads the diagram body as mermaid@12 handed it to its lexer: front
matter and `%%{…}%%` directives removed; CRLF and CR read as LF; `="x"` inside an HTML tag read
as `='x'`; `%%` comment lines removed and leading blanks trimmed; on a line with
`style…:…#…;` (or `classDef…`) the last `;` dropped; `#name;` / `#123;` entities read as
opaque text; and a line break appended. Keywords are case-sensitive.

**Line breaks are skipped.** Nothing ends a row: two rows may share a line, and a row may run
over lines. A row's indent is the run of blanks right before its name, wherever it is, so a
blank at the end of a line indents the row on the next line, and a second blank run before an
indented row is an error. The first rule that matches wins and no rule gives way to a longer
one: `treemapx` is `treemap` and the name `x`, `titleX` is a title and `X`.

## Grammar

EBNF: `[ x ]` is optional, `{ x }` repeats zero or more times, `x+` one or more times, `|` separates alternatives. Upper-case names and `subgraph`, `end`, `acc_…`, `direction_…` are tokens (see below). A rule marked `@Type` builds an AST node of that type.

```ebnf
treemap = Header { text | row } EOF ;
```

`treemap` or `treemap-beta`: starts a treemap.

```ebnf
Header @Header = TREEMAP_KEYWORD ;
```

```ebnf
text = Title
     | AccTitle
     | AccDescr ;
```

A row: its indent, then a section, a leaf or a `classDef`. Rows nest by indent: a row goes
under the nearest section before it with a smaller indent, or at the top.

```ebnf
row = [ INDENTATION ] ( Section | Leaf | ClassDef ) ;
```

`"Name"` or `"Name":::class`: a section, whose value is the sum of the leaves under it.

```ebnf
Section @Section = STRING [ STYLE_SEPARATOR ID ] ;
```

`"Name": 10` or `"Name", 10` (and `:::class`): a leaf and its value.

```ebnf
Leaf @Leaf = STRING [ INDENTATION ] ( SEPARATOR | COMMA ) [ INDENTATION ] NUMBER [ STYLE_SEPARATOR ID ] ;
```

`classDef name styles;`: a class of styles that rows take with `:::name`; a repeat adds
styles.

```ebnf
ClassDef @ClassDef = CLASS_DEF ;
```

`title Budget`: the title drawn above the treemap (the last one wins).

```ebnf
Title @Title = TITLE ;
```

`accTitle: …`: the accessible title.

```ebnf
AccTitle @AccTitle = ACC_TITLE ;
```

`accDescr: …` or `accDescr { … }`: the accessible description.

```ebnf
AccDescr @AccDescr = ACC_DESCR ;
```

## Tokens

The lexer works in modes (`INITIAL` and the ones below). In each mode it tries the rules in this order and takes the first that matches; a rule may push a mode or pop back to the previous one. Rules without a token emit nothing.

Modes: `INITIAL`.

| Modes | Token | Pattern | Action | Doc |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| INITIAL | ACC_DESCR | `[\t ]*accDescr[\t ]*:(?:[^\n\r]*?(?=%%)\|[^\n\r]*)` |  | `accDescr: …` (the rest of the line) or `accDescr { … }` (over lines, to `}`): the accessible description of the diagram. mermaid@12's one rule, as two tried in order; the block's `[\s\S]*?\}` is its `[^}]*\}`, written so that line-based highlighters read the block as one span. |
| INITIAL | ACC_DESCR | `[\t ]*accDescr\s*\{[\s\S]*?\}` |  |  |
| INITIAL | ACC_TITLE | `[\t ]*accTitle[\t ]*:(?:[^\n\r]*?(?=%%)\|[^\n\r]*)` |  | `accTitle: …`: the accessible title of the diagram, the rest of the line. |
| INITIAL | TITLE | `[\t ]*title(?:[\t ][^\n\r]*?(?=%%)\|[\t ][^\n\r]*\|)` |  | `title …`: the title drawn above the treemap, the rest of the line (the last one wins). |
| INITIAL | TREEMAP_KEYWORD | `treemap-beta\|treemap` |  | `treemap` or `treemap-beta`: starts a treemap. |
| INITIAL | CLASS_DEF | `classDef\s+[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]+(?:\s+[^;\r\n]*)?;?` |  | `classDef name styles;`: a class of styles (`fill:#f96,stroke:#333`) that rows take with `:::name`. The name has two characters or more; the styles run to `;` or the line end, and with none on its line the next line is read as them. A repeat adds styles. |
| INITIAL | STYLE_SEPARATOR | `:::` |  | `:::name`: the class of a row, right after its name or value. |
| INITIAL | SEPARATOR | `:` |  |  |
| INITIAL | COMMA | `,` |  |  |
| INITIAL | INDENTATION | `[\t ]+` |  | A run of blanks: the indent of the row whose name follows it. |
| INITIAL | COMMENT | `%%[^\n]*` |  | `%%` to the end of the line, after other text: a comment. |
| INITIAL | — | `\n` |  |  |
| INITIAL | ID | `[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*` |  | A class name: ASCII letters, digits and `_`, not starting with a digit. |
| INITIAL | NUMBER | `[0-9_.,]+` |  | A value: digits, `.`, `,` and `_`, read as a number with the commas removed (`1,000` is 1000; `1_000` is 1). |
| INITIAL | STRING | `"[^"]*"\|'[^']*'` |  | A name: `"…"` or `'…'`, with no escapes; a name may span lines. |
| INITIAL | EOF | `$` |  | The end of the text. |

Removed before lexing (highlighted only):

- COMMENT: `^[^\S\n]*%%(?!\{)[^\n]+`
- DIRECTIVE: `[^\S\n]*%%\{[\s\S]*?\}%%`
